 College basketball rankings: Michigan State jumps in AP Top 25 after win vs. Duke; Kentucky drops out of poll
 The Spartans made a big move in the second AP Top 25 of the regular season
 By
 Cameron Salerno 
 Nov 16, 2026
 at
 1:07 pm ET 
 •
 3 min read
 Getty Images 
 For the first time this season, there was a significant shakeup in the AP Top 25 poll released Monday after just one team ranked inside the top 10 of the preseason poll lost during the first week. Among the highlights of last week: Michigan State recording a wire-to-wire win over Duke, Kansas flexing its muscles during a win over Kentucky in the second leg of the Champions Classic and Texas Tech taking down Illinois at home.
 And that was just the games that happened on Tuesday.
 On Sunday, there was another upset from a top-10 team. After leading by as many as 18 points against Memphis, Louisville lost by 20. As a result, the Cardinals dropped 13 spots down to No. 23.
 Michigan State is one of the biggest winners of this week's poll, jumping three spots all the way to No. 2, ahead of UConn. The Spartans have a key matchup looming against No. 14 Tennessee this week, which should be a great measuring stick for both teams heading into mid-November.
 Mark Pope says he hopes Kentucky fans 'had fun' after near historic upset as a 34.5-point favorite vs. NAU 
 Cameron Salerno 
 After opening the season ranked No. 23, it took just two weeks for Kentucky to fall out of the poll entirely. The Wildcats lost to Kansas 89-69 in the Champions Classic and nearly lost to Northern Arizona at home as a 34.5-point favorite, which would've gone down as one of the worst losses in program history. Kentucky guard Alex Wilkins saved the day with a 3-pointer with 2.2 seconds remaining to avoid disaster in a 78-77 victory, but the voters predictably still didn't include UK in this week's poll.
 LSU, which had a chaotic offseason under coach Will Wade, joined the rankings at No. 25.
 College basketball Top 25 rankings: Duke, Louisville fall in week 2 Coaches Poll after spotlight losses 
 Brad Crawford 
 Here is this week's full poll, with the latest rankings.
 AP Top 25

 Also receiving votes : Memphis 172, Texas A&M 31, Iowa State 30, Kentucky 17, TCU 14, Baylor 11, High Point 9, Saint Louis 8, Xavier 6, Santa Clara 3, Notre Dame 3, Minnesota 2, Utah State 2, North Carolina 1 
 Duke only drops three spots after loss to Spartans
 Duke wasn't punished much for losing to Michigan State last week and only dropped three spots to No. 5 in this week's poll. Meanwhile, Illinois dropped seven spots to No. 10  — rightfully behind No. 9 Texas Tech — in this week's poll after losing to the Red Raiders on the road. Although the Blue Devils vs. Illini matchup Tuesday won't be No. 2 vs. No. 3 as it was in the preseason rankings, it's going to be one of the biggest of the nonconference season. It also marks Duke's latest test, with matchups against UConn and Florida also looming over the next few weeks. The Blue Devils have the toughest noncofrnece schedule of any Division l team. 
 Welcome to the party, LSU 
 Maybe there was a method to Will Wade's madness. LSU pulled off one of the biggest wins of the season on the road against Gonzaga behind a last-second, go-ahead 3-pointer by Donovan Dent . Dent is one of a handful of players on the roster playing this season on a temporary injection, which clears the way for him to play a fifth season of college basketball. Dent has been fantastic so far for LSU. The Tigers are a dangerous team at full strength. After being picked to finish 14th in the preseason SEC media poll, this is definitely a team that will outperform expectations. 
 Tomorrow's Top 25 Today: Michigan State makes huge jump after win over Duke in rankings prediction 
 Cameron Salerno 
 Rough week for Bluegrass State 
 Last week was rough for the Bluegrass State. Kentucky lost to Kansas in the Champions Classic and were almost on the wrong side of what would've been one of the biggest upsets (34.5-point favorite) in college basketball history. Louisville led by as many as 18 points against Memphis but ultimately lost by 20. Kentucky dropped out of the poll, while Louisville was the biggest dropper of the week, moving down 13 spots to No. 23. Kentucky still received 17 votes this week, which is surprising after watching both games last week.
